data.narrative:
Verdant Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Gabe Sibley and Curtis Garner, having raised $58M to date. The valuation analysis benchmarks against a comp universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public company, with peer valuations ranging from $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed stage) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $58M total raised as a proxy base value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression, implies a valuation of $116M. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector and same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $2.0B. This reflects heterogeneity in the peer set—three Series B companies ($1.8B–$2.0B), one Series A peer at $1.4B, and one Seed-stage peer at $1.1B.

The two methods produce materially different outputs, yielding a triangulated range of $99M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $883M. The wide dispersion reflects uncertainty around stage-appropriate valuation anchors and peer comparability. The stage-progression method appears conservative relative to peer multiples; the peer-median may overweight later-stage or better-capitalized comparables. Key uncertainties include the appropriate discount for Verdant's Series A status relative to Series B peers, and whether the peer set adequately reflects similar technology maturity and market traction.
